source.text: Καὶ ἐπὶ τούτῳ ἦλθαν οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐθαύμαζον ὅτι μετὰ γυναικὸς ἐλάλει· οὐδεὶς μέντοι εἶπεν· Τί ζητεῖς;

records.literal_gloss: And upon this came the disciples of him, and they were marveling that with a woman he was speaking; no one however said, "What do you seek?"

en.L: And at this [moment] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples came, and they were marveling that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} seeking?"
en.B: At that moment {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples arrived, and they were astonished that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was speaking with a woman. Yet none of them said, "What are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} looking for?"
en.R: Right then Jesus's disciples came back. They were amazed that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was talking with a woman. But none of them asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "What do {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want from her?"

es.L: Y en esto llegaron sus discípulos, y se maravillaban de que hablara con una mujer; sin embargo, nadie dijo: «¿Qué buscas?»
es.B: En ese momento llegaron sus discípulos, y se quedaron asombrados de que estuviera hablando con una mujer. Pero ninguno le dijo: «¿Qué buscas?»
es.R: Justo entonces volvieron los discípulos de Jesús. Se sorprendieron de que hablara con una mujer. Pero ninguno le preguntó: «¿Qué quieres de ella?»

fr.L: Et sur ce, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples arrivèrent, et ils s’étonnaient de ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} parlait avec une femme ; pourtant personne ne dit : « Que cherches-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.B: À ce moment-là, {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples arrivèrent, et ils s’étonnèrent de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir parler avec une femme. Pourtant aucun d’eux ne dit : « Que cherches-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} ? »
fr.R: Juste à ce moment-là, les disciples de Jésus sont revenus. Ils ont été très surpris de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} voir parler avec une femme. Mais aucun d’eux ne {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a demandé : « Qu’est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lui demandes ? »

sw.L: Na wakati huo wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wakaja, nao wakastaajabu kwamba alikuwa akizungumza na mwanamke; lakini hakuna aliyesema, "Unatafuta nini?"
sw.B: Wakati huo huo wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walifika, wakashangaa kwamba alikuwa akizungumza na mwanamke. Hata hivyo hakuna aliyemwuliza, "Unatafuta nini?"
sw.R: Wakati huo huo wanafunzi wa Yesu walirudi. Walishangaa kwamba alikuwa akizungumza na mwanamke. Lakini hakuna aliyemwuliza, "Unataka nini kwake?"

vi.L: Vừa lúc ấy các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến, và họ ngạc nhiên vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang nói chuyện với một người phụ nữ; nhưng không ai nói: "Thầy tìm gì?"
vi.B: Ngay lúc đó các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} về tới, và họ rất ngạc nhiên vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang nói chuyện với một người phụ nữ. Nhưng không ai hỏi: "Thầy cần gì?"
vi.R: Ngay lúc ấy các môn đồ của Đức Giê-xu trở về. Họ lấy làm lạ vì {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang nói chuyện với một người phụ nữ. Nhưng không ai hỏi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thầy muốn gì ở chị ấy?"

ko.L: 그리고 이때에 그분의 제자들이 왔고, 그분이 여자와 말씀하고 계신 것을 이상히 여기고 있었다. 그러나 아무도 "무엇을 찾으십니까?" 하고 말하지 않았고,
ko.B: 바로 그때 제자들이 돌아왔다. 그들은 예수께서 여자와 이야기하고 계신 것을 보고 놀랐다. 그러나 아무도 "무엇을 찾으십니까?" 하고 묻지 않았고,
ko.R: 바로 그때 예수의 제자들이 돌아왔다. 제자들은 예수께서 여자와 이야기하고 계신 것을 보고 놀랐다. 그러나 아무도 "이 여자에게 무엇을 원하십니까?" 하고 묻지 않았고,

decisions.choice: at this: just as Jesus said "I am he" (4:26)
decisions.reason: The phrase marks the moment. The disciples, who had gone into the town to buy food (4:8), come back at the very point where Jesus has told the woman who he is, and the conversation ends.

decisions.choice: they were surprised that a teacher was talking in public with a woman
alternatives: surprised only that she was a Samaritan
decisions.reason: John says "a woman", not "a Samaritan": the surprise is that a teacher was talking alone with a woman he did not know. Jewish teaching of the time was wary of this; the Mishnah, collected about AD 200, records the saying "do not talk much with a woman" (Avot 1:5). That she was also a Samaritan (4:9) made it stranger still. The imperfect verb pictures their surprise as lasting while they took in the scene.

decisions.choice: both questions are ones they might have put to Jesus, and did not
alternatives: the first question is to the woman (what do you want?), the second to Jesus
decisions.reason: The verbs are singular, and the second question, "why are you speaking with her?", is plainly to Jesus; joined by "or", the two are most naturally alternatives put to the same person. μέντοι ("yet") shows that respect for their teacher kept them quiet. "What are you seeking?" is the question Jesus himself asked the first disciples (1:38).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "you" when people speak to him, as here, even though the question is not spoken aloud. At the start of a sentence "He" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: What are you looking for? (B); What do you want from her? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same everyday words as at 1:38, so the echo stays visible; Readable says plainly what the question would have meant here and supplies "from her", which the scene implies.

decisions.choice: ¿Qué buscas? (L, B); ¿Qué quieres de ella? (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the same words as at 1:38 ("¿Qué buscan?"), so the echo stays visible; Readable says plainly what the question would have meant here.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("dit"); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
alternatives: passé composé for narration at every level
the present tense throughout at Literal
decisions.reason: The French brief for the whole passage (4:27-54). The passé simple ("arrivèrent", "crurent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present (4:28, 4:34, 4:49, 4:50 "dit"), as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("les disciples sont revenus"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first. Inside speech every level uses the passé composé ("il m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait"). The imperfect ("s’étonnaient", "priaient") is used at every level for what was going on.

decisions.choice: Qu’est-ce que tu lui demandes ? (R)
decisions.reason: English Readable says what the question would have meant here ("What do you want from her?"). The French idiom "Qu’est-ce que tu lui veux ?" sounds hostile, as if Jesus meant her harm; "Qu’est-ce que tu lui demandes ?" is plain and fits the scene, since Jesus had asked her for a drink (4:7).

decisions.choice: disciples call Jesus "Thầy", with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets out, the disciples address Jesus as "Thầy" (Teacher) and speak of themselves as "chúng con"; "Thầy" is a noun of address, always capitalised, so it takes no setting.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; "그분", "께서" and the honorific "-시-" carry the respect
alternatives: a deity_pronoun span around "그분" (it would have nothing to change)
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change and the Korean text has no such spans in this passage. Respect for Jesus is carried at every level by the honorific forms.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends with a comma, and "no one said" is completed in the next sentence
alternatives: repeat the full clause "아무도 ... 묻지 않았다" in both sentences
decisions.reason: Korean puts the verb after the quotation, so "no one said" must follow the first question; the second question (its own sentence in the SBLGNT) then takes its own "하고 묻지도 않았다".

source.text: ἢ τί λαλεῖς μετ’ αὐτῆς;

records.literal_gloss: Or why do you speak with her?

en.L: or, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speaking with her?"
en.B: or, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} speaking with her?"
en.R: or, "Why are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} talking with her?"

es.L: o: «¿Por qué hablas con ella?».
es.B: ni: «¿Por qué hablas con ella?».
es.R: ni: «¿Por qué estás hablando con ella?».

fr.L: ou : « Pourquoi parles-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avec elle ? »
fr.B: ni : « Pourquoi parles-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} avec elle ? »
fr.R: ni : « Pourquoi est-ce que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} parles avec elle ? »

sw.L: au, "Mbona unazungumza naye?"
sw.B: au, "Kwa nini unazungumza naye?"
sw.R: au, "Kwa nini unazungumza naye?"

vi.L: hoặc: "Sao Thầy nói chuyện với chị ấy?"
vi.B: hoặc: "Sao Thầy nói chuyện với chị ấy?"
vi.R: hoặc: "Sao Thầy lại nói chuyện với chị ấy?"

ko.L: 또는 "왜 그 여자와 말씀하십니까?" [하고 말하지도 않았다].
ko.B: "왜 그 여자와 이야기하십니까?" 하고 묻지도 않았다.
ko.R: "왜 이 여자와 이야기하십니까?" 하고 묻지도 않았다.

decisions.choice: a second question, its own sentence in the SBLGNT but still governed by "no one said"
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT ends the first question with a question mark and begins this one with "or", so the record starts in the middle of the reported speech. Both questions belong to what the disciples did not say; the renderings begin in lower case so that the two records read as one sentence.

decisions.choice: ni (B, R); o (L)
decisions.reason: After "ninguno le dijo", Spanish joins the second question with "ni"; Literal keeps the Greek "or".

decisions.choice: ni (B, R); ou (L)
decisions.reason: The question is still governed by "no one said" (meaning decision m1). After a negative French joins the second question with "ni"; Literal keeps "ou", the Greek word.

decisions.choice: "하고 말하지도 않았다" (L, in brackets); "하고 묻지도 않았다" (B, R)
alternatives: leave the question without a verb
decisions.reason: The Greek verb "said" stands once, before both questions; Korean must close each quotation with a verb, so it is repeated here, in brackets at Literal. The disciples would have spoken to Jesus in 합쇼체.

source.text: ἀφῆκεν οὖν τὴν ὑδρίαν αὐτῆς ἡ γυνὴ καὶ ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὴν πόλιν καὶ λέγει τοῖς ἀνθρώποις·

sw.L: Basi yule mwanamke akauacha mtungi wake, akaenda zake mjini, naye anawaambia watu,
sw.B: Kisha yule mwanamke aliuacha mtungi wake, akarudi mjini, akawaambia watu,
sw.R: Yule mwanamke aliuacha mtungi wake hapo, akarudi mjini haraka. Akawaambia watu wa huko,

vi.L: Vậy người phụ nữ bỏ vò nước của mình lại, đi vào thành, và nói với mọi người:
vi.B: Rồi người phụ nữ bỏ vò nước lại, trở vào thành và nói với mọi người:
vi.R: Người phụ nữ để vò nước lại đó và vội vàng trở về thành. Chị nói với mọi người ở đó:

ko.L: 그러자 그 여자는 자기 물동이를 버려두고 마을로 들어가서 사람들에게 말한다.
ko.B: 그러자 그 여자는 물동이를 놓아둔 채 마을로 돌아가서 사람들에게 말했다.
ko.R: 여자는 물동이를 거기 두고 서둘러 마을로 돌아갔다. 그리고 그곳 사람들에게 말했다.

decisions.choice: she left the jar behind as she went off to the town
alternatives: a deliberate sign that she no longer cares for well water (4:13-15)
decisions.reason: She came to draw water (4:7), and now she leaves the jar at the well, perhaps in haste and meaning to come back. Some readers see a picture in it: she has found the living water Jesus spoke of (4:10-14). John does not say so, so every level simply reports it.

decisions.choice: the town: Sychar (4:5)
decisions.reason: The word is used of any walled or settled place, small or large. Here it is Sychar, the town near Jacob's well (4:5).

decisions.choice: the people of the town, men and women
alternatives: only the men, gathered in a public place
decisions.reason: The plural of this word is the ordinary term for people in general; it does not mark them as male. Those she speaks to are the townspeople who then come out (4:30) and of whom many believe (4:39-42).

decisions.choice: the {{gender:people|men}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general (meaning decision m3), so the inclusive word is the default and the gender setting gives the traditional "men".

decisions.choice: said
decisions.reason: John often tells a story in the present tense ("she says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as stories are normally told in this language. This applies to every such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: town
decisions.reason: Sychar was a small place (meaning decision m2); "city" would suggest something much larger.

decisions.choice: hurried back
decisions.reason: Readable shows the haste implied by her leaving the jar and going at once.

decisions.choice: historic present at Literal; pretérito at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in John: Literal keeps John's present ("llega", "le dice"); Balanced and Readable use the pretérito. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: {{gender:la gente|los hombres}}
decisions.reason: The word means people in general (meaning decision m3): inclusive default, traditional one tap away.

decisions.choice: cántaro
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the one used for the stone jars of 2:6, which Spanish calls "tinajas". Here it is the jar she carried to the well, which Spanish calls a "cántaro".

decisions.choice: la ville
decisions.reason: French "ville" names any town, small or large, and is the plain word for a place like Sychar (meaning decision m2); "village" would make it smaller than the Greek says, and "bourgade" is literary. The same word is used through the passage (4:30, 4:39).

decisions.choice: une cruche
decisions.reason: A cruche is the jug a woman carried to the well; "jarre" is kept for the large stone jars of 2:6.

decisions.choice: "mọi người" with no gender span
alternatives: a gender span as in the English
decisions.reason: "mọi người" (everyone) already includes men and women; Vietnamese has no second wording for the setting to choose.

decisions.choice: historic present: Literal "nói" without "đã"; the other levels tell it as past where Vietnamese needs it
decisions.reason: Vietnamese verbs do not mark tense, so John's historic present shows only in Literal leaving out "đã"; one decision for the passage.

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("말한다", "말씀하신다"); past at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: As the guide asks, Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as Korean narrative does. One decision for the passage. "사람들" includes men and women, so there is no gender span.

source.text: Δεῦτε ἴδετε ἄνθρωπον ὃς εἶπέ μοι πάντα ὅσα ἐποίησα· μήτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;

records.literal_gloss: "Come, see a man who told me all things as many as I did; can it be that this one is the Christ?"

en.L: "Come, see a man who told me all the things that I did. Can it be that this [man] is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"
en.B: "Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Could this possibly be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"
en.R: "Come and see a man who told me all the things I have ever done! Might {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?"

es.L: «{{plural_you:Vengan, vean|Venid, ved}} a un hombre que me dijo todo lo que he hecho. ¿Acaso será este el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.B: «{{plural_you:Vengan a ver|Venid a ver}} a un hombre que me ha dicho todo lo que he hecho. ¿No será este el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».
es.R: «¡{{plural_you:Vengan a ver|Venid a ver}} a un hombre que me dijo todo lo que he hecho en mi vida! ¿Será {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?».

fr.L: « Venez, voyez un homme qui m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait. Se pourrait-il que celui-ci soit le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ? »
fr.B: « Venez voir un homme qui m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait. Se pourrait-il vraiment que ce soit le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ? »
fr.R: « Venez voir un homme qui m’a dit tout ce que j’ai fait dans ma vie ! Est-ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} serait le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} ? »

sw.L: "Njooni, mwone mtu aliyeniambia mambo yote niliyoyafanya. Je, yawezekana huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.B: "Njooni mwone mtu aliyeniambia kila kitu nilichowahi kufanya. Inawezekana huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"
sw.R: "Njooni mwone mtu aliyeniambia mambo yote niliyowahi kufanya! Huenda {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?"

vi.L: "Hãy đến xem một người đã nói với tôi mọi điều tôi đã làm. Phải chăng người này là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}?"
vi.B: "Hãy đến mà xem một người đã nói cho tôi biết mọi việc tôi đã làm. Có thể nào người ấy là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} không?"
vi.R: "Mọi người hãy đến xem một người đã nói cho tôi biết mọi việc tôi từng làm! Có lẽ nào ông ấy là {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}?"

ko.L: "와서 제가 한 모든 일을 저에게 말한 사람을 보십시오. 혹시 이 사람이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}가 아니겠습니까?"
ko.B: "와서 보십시오. 제가 한 일을 모두 저에게 말해 준 사람이 있습니다. 혹시 이분이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}가 아니겠습니까?"
ko.R: "와서 보십시오! 제가 지금까지 한 일을 모두 말해 준 사람이 있습니다! 혹시 그분이 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}가 아니겠습니까?"

decisions.choice: everything I have done: an overstatement that sums up her life
alternatives: a full list of her deeds
decisions.reason: Jesus had told her about her five husbands and the man she now lived with (4:16-18). That he knew this was enough to show he knew her whole life. Her words also echo what she said of the Messiah: "he will tell us all things" (4:25).

decisions.choice: a hesitant question that hopes but does not claim: could this be the Christ?
alternatives: a question expecting yes: is not this the Christ?
a question expecting no: this cannot be the Christ
decisions.reason: μήτι normally introduces a question that expects "no" (as in 4:33). Here, as in Matthew 12:23, it voices a guarded hope: she does not dare to assert it, but she raises it so that others will come and judge for themselves. The renderings keep the question tentative. Some older versions turned it into a confident "Is not this the Christ?", which the form does not support.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the title, the Anointed One she has just spoken of (4:25)
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title. The woman herself used the Hebrew word Messiah, which John translates (4:25). Samaritans accepted only the five books of Moses, and their hope rested on the promise of a prophet like Moses (Deuteronomy 18:15-18); later Samaritan writings speak of a coming restorer who would reveal the truth.

decisions.choice: Come, see: she invites others as Philip invited Nathanael
decisions.reason: The two plural commands repeat the pattern of 1:39 and 1:46, "come and see": the one who has met Jesus brings others to see for themselves. The woman becomes the first witness to Jesus in Samaria (4:39).

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, so every level writes "the" outside the span, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: Could this possibly be ...? (B); Might he be ...? (R)
alternatives: He cannot be the Christ, can he?
decisions.reason: These keep the hesitation of the question (meaning decision m2) without turning it into a denial or a confession.

decisions.choice: ¿Acaso será ...? (L); ¿No será ...? (B); ¿Será él ...? (R)
decisions.reason: These keep the hesitation of the question (meaning decision m2): "¿No será...?" voices a guarded hope in everyday Spanish, without turning it into a denial or a confession.

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: Se pourrait-il que ... ? (L, B); Est-ce qu’il serait ... ? (R)
decisions.reason: The question hopes without claiming (meaning decision m2). French "Ne serait-ce pas ... ?" expects the answer yes and turns it into a quiet confession; "Se pourrait-il que ... ?" and the conditional "serait" keep it open.

decisions.choice: the woman addresses the townspeople in 합쇼체 ("보십시오", "제가", "저에게")
decisions.reason: She speaks to the people of the town as a group, and 합쇼체 is the polite public address; the humble "저" fits a woman of low standing speaking to them.

decisions.choice: "혹시 ... 아니겠습니까?" for the hesitant question
decisions.reason: "혹시" with a negative question hopes for yes without claiming it, which is how the meaning decision reads the Greek; "-일 수 있겠습니까?" would sound doubtful.

decisions.choice: no connecting word (SBLGNT)

decisions.choice: were urging him: kept asking him to eat
decisions.reason: The verb usually means "ask", and it can mean a request as well as a question. Here what follows is a request, and the imperfect shows them pressing it more than once.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: the respectful title for a teacher
decisions.reason: The disciples use the title John explained at 1:38. They had gone to the town for food (4:8) and now offer it to him.

decisions.choice: Rabbi
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for John: John translates the word himself (1:38), so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: something (B, R); please (R)
decisions.reason: A bare "eat" sounds abrupt; the words give the friendly tone of the disciples' request.

decisions.choice: algo (B, R); por favor (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: a bare "come" sounds abrupt; the words give the friendly tone. "Rabí" at every level, as at 1:38.

decisions.choice: "랍비" (L); "랍비님" (B, R); the disciples speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 ("잡수십시오")

decisions.choice: you do not know: you have no knowledge of it

decisions.choice: you are not aware of (B); you do not know about (R)
decisions.reason: "Know" with "food" as its object is unnatural here; these say what it means (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: que ustedes no conocen
decisions.reason: English needs "not aware of", but Spanish "conocer" takes a thing as its object naturally, so every level keeps the verb (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: Moi, j’ai ... vous, vous ne connaissez pas (L)
alternatives: J’ai ... que vous ne connaissez pas
decisions.reason: French marks the emphatic pronouns of the Greek (meaning decision m1) with the stressed forms "moi" and "vous, vous"; Balanced and Readable leave the contrast to the sentence.

decisions.choice: Jesus to his disciples: "Ta" and "các con"

decisions.choice: a puzzled question that expects no

decisions.choice: they take his words about food literally

decisions.choice: Did someone bring him food while we were gone?

decisions.reason: Readable asks the question plainly and adds "while we were gone", which the story implies (4:8); the puzzled tone remains.

decisions.choice: ¿Alguien le trajo comida mientras no estábamos?

decisions.choice: what sustains Jesus is doing the Father's will
decisions.reason: Food gives life and strength; Jesus says his life is fed by obedience. The thought is like Deuteronomy 8:3, that people do not live by bread alone. Later he says, "I have come down from heaven not to do my own will but the will of him who sent me" (6:38).

decisions.choice: the one who sent me: God the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus often describes God as "the one who sent me" (5:24, 30; 6:38-39; 7:16). It presents him as the Father's envoy, who speaks and acts for the one who sent him.

decisions.choice: complete: carry through to the end
decisions.reason: The verb means to bring something to its goal. Jesus uses it again in his prayer, "I have completed the work you gave me to do" (17:4), and from the cross he says "It is finished" (19:30), from the same root.

decisions.choice: doing ... bringing ... to completion
alternatives: that I should do ... and complete (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the purpose clause into a plain description of what his food is.

decisions.choice: what God wants. He sent me
alternatives: the will of the one who sent me
decisions.reason: Readable names God, whom "the one who sent me" means (meaning decision m2), and splits the long phrase into short sentences.

decisions.choice: lo que Dios quiere. Él me envió
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names God (meaning decision m2) and splits the long phrase. "Él" begins a sentence and is written plain.

decisions.choice: le travail qu’il m’a confié (R)
decisions.reason: In the short Readable sentence "finir son travail" could be read as Jesus's own work; "le travail qu’il m’a confié" makes clear that the work is God's (meaning decision m2).
